nits.summary: When BLK-B gets rewritten, the claim '0-elem %w is a no-op' is itself wrong on box 3.3.8: system(%w[]) RAISES ArgumentError: wrong first argument (identical to the 1-elem case). Write '0- and 1-element %w/%i under system all raise ArgumentError ⇒ dead ⇒ silence safe', not 'no-op'.

The complement enumeration should cover , = ! : too (all 0 rows in my probe) even though only >/;/|/& (+| pipe-into, already in BLK-A) are shell-live word splitters — naming the FULL class 'any char outside [\s(\[{<] and not a quote-then-slash pair' (which is what the matcher actually implements) is smaller than enumerating characters and immune to the next round adding a char to my probe set.

The dq spelling 'x"/usr' shows 0 rows only because the verb span truncates at the closing quote — the quote-adjacent case is boundary-class-adjacent to ABSOLUTE_LITERAL in the pctq/backtick spellings (1 row). A named-class doc sentence should not conflate c=" with the rest of the complement without noting the span-truncation nuance.

/usr/local/bin is root-owned and NOT writable by user lab on this box; any doc sentence claiming files 'materialize under /usr/local/bin' on this box should instead cite the rooted dir actually used for the proof (my replication used /tmp/…/live and got REDIR_GT/REDIR_BT/QOPEN_OK materialized).
